chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Bakir, from Zurarah, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and heard him start the prayer with seven continuous Takbirs.
ai.seo_question: How many Takbirs did the Imam use to start his prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* highlights the practice of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in performing seven consecutive Takbirs at the start of prayer, a detail often discussed in the context of the differences between Shia and Sunni jurisprudence regarding the number of opening Takbirs. The chain of transmission, featuring prominent figures like Ibn Abi Umair and Zurarah, underscores the reliability of this report within the Shia scholarly tradition. This practice reflects a specific liturgical emphasis on the magnification of God at the commencement of worship, distinct from the single Takbir commonly observed in other schools of thought.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-18 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Bakir that Zurarah said,
“I saw Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) and heard him start his prayer with seven continuous Takbirs (saying God is Great).”
